hints: Think about what must stay exactly the same for two compounds to be isomers, count atoms of each element.
Think about what must be different, how the atoms are joined or arranged in the displayed structure.
walkthrough:
Separate same from different**
Isomerism is a same and different idea. The same part is the molecular formula. That means both molecules contain exactly the same numbers of C and H atoms, for example both are $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$. If the atom count differs, they cannot be isomers.

Pin down what changes**
The different part is how those atoms are connected. Structural isomers have a different order of bonding, so their structural or displayed formulae are different. That is why combustion data cannot tell them apart, burning counts atoms but does not see connectivity.

Final answer: Molecules with the same molecular formula / same number of atoms of each element.
But with different structural / displayed formulae / different arrangement of atoms / bonds.

hints: Use the volume drop on treatment with alkali, $150 \text{ cm}^3$ to $50 \text{ cm}^3$, to find the volume of $\text{CO}_2$ formed from $25 \text{ cm}^3$ of P.
walkthrough:
Find the volume of $\text{CO}_2$**
After combustion the gas is $\text{CO}_2$ + leftover $\text{O}_2$ = $150 \text{ cm}^3$. Alkali absorbs all the $\text{CO}_2$, leaving only leftover $\text{O}_2$ = $50 \text{ cm}^3$. So: $$V(\text{CO}_2) = 150 - 50 = 100 \text{ cm}^3$$
Remember water is liquid, so it contributes no volume.

Link gas volume to $x$**
At same T and p, volume ratio equals mole ratio. From the equation, $1$ volume of $\text{C}_x\text{H}_y$ gives $x$ volumes of $\text{CO}_2$: $$x \times 25 = 100$$ $$x = 4$$

hints: Find the volume of $\text{O}_2$ actually used by subtracting the leftover $\text{O}_2$ from the initial $200 \text{ cm}^3$, then relate it to $(x + y/4)$ volumes per volume of P.
walkthrough:
Find the volume of $\text{O}_2$ used**
You started with $200 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{O}_2$. After alkali treatment $50 \text{ cm}^3$ remains, so that $50 \text{ cm}^3$ is unused excess: $$V(\text{O}_2 \text{ used}) = 200 - 50 = 150 \text{ cm}^3$$

Link to the equation coefficient**
One volume of P uses $(x + y/4)$ volumes of $\text{O}_2$. So for $25 \text{ cm}^3$ of P: $$(x + y/4) \times 25 = 150$$ $$(x + y/4) = 150 / 25 = 6$$

hints: Combine your values $x = 4$ and $(x + y/4) = 6$ to solve for $y$ and write the full $\text{C}_x\text{H}_y$ formula.
Recall that empirical formula is the simplest whole number ratio, so divide the subscripts by their highest common factor.
walkthrough:
Solve for $y$**
You know $x = 4$ and $x + y/4 = 6$. Substitute: $$4 + y/4 = 6$$ $$y/4 = 2$$ $$y = 8$$ So the molecular formula is $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8}$.

Simplify to empirical**
Empirical means simplest ratio. $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8}$ divides by $4$: $$\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8} \rightarrow \text{CH}_{2}$$ This makes sense for an alkene.

Final answer: molecular formula of P = $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8}$
empirical formula of P = $\text{CH}_{2}$

hints: Since P is $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8}$ unbranched, draw a straight four carbon chain with one C=C double bond and think where that bond can sit.
Recall skeletal formulae use lines for carbon skeleton with no C or H labels, and positional isomers differ only in the position of the functional group.
walkthrough:
Recognise the family**
$\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8}$ fits $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$, so P is an alkene with one double bond. Unbranched means a straight chain of four carbons, no side methyl branch.

Move the double bond**
Positional isomers keep the same skeleton but move the position of the double bond. Option 1 is but-1-ene: $$\text{CH}_{2}\text{=CH-CH}_{2}\text{-CH}_{3}$$ In skeletal form this is a zigzag of three lines with a double line at one end. Option 2 is but-2-ene: $$\text{CH}_{3}\text{-CH=CH-CH}_{3}$$ In skeletal form the double line is in the middle of the zigzag. Both are valid and are positional isomers of each other.

Final answer: Skeletal structure of but-1-ene: $\text{CH}_{2}\text{=CHCH}_{2}\text{CH}_{3}$ drawn as skeletal: two-carbon double line joined to two single lines.
Skeletal structure of but-2-ene: $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH=CHCH}_{3}$ drawn as skeletal: single line, double line in middle, single line.

hints: List $p$, $V$ and $T$ for the original sample and convert them to SI units: Pa, $\text{m}^3$ and K.
Rearrange $pV = nRT$ to $n = pV/RT$ to find the moles of P in $25 \text{ cm}^3$.
Convert moles to mass using $m = n \times M_r$ with $M_r(\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8}) = 56.0$, giving the answer to three significant figures.
walkthrough:
Convert to SI units**
The gas equation needs Pa, $\text{m}^3$ and K. Do this first: $$p = 100 \text{ kPa} = 100 \times 10^{3} \text{ Pa}$$ $$V = 25 \text{ cm}^3 = 25 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$$ $$T = 37 + 273 = 310 \text{ K}$$ A common slip is to use $\text{cm}^3$ directly, that gives a hugely wrong answer.

Calculate moles with $pV = nRT$**
Rearrange to $n = pV/RT$: $$n = \frac{100 \times 10^{3} \times 25 \times 10^{-6}}{8.31 \times 310}$$ $$n = 9.705 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$$ Keep extra figures for now to avoid rounding error.

Convert moles to mass**
$M_r$ of $\text{C}_{4}\text{H}_{8} = (4 \times 12.0) + (8 \times 1.0) = 56.0$. Use $m = n \times M_r$: $$m = 9.705 \times 10^{-4} \times 56.0 = 0.0543 \text{ g}$$ Give to three significant figures with unit g, as requested.

Final answer: $p = 100 \text{ kPa} = 100000 \text{ Pa}$; $V = 25 \text{ cm}^3 = 25 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$; $T = 37 + 273 = 310 \text{ K}$
$n = pV/RT = (100 \times 10^{3} \times 25 \times 10^{-6})/(8.31 \times 310) = 9.71 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$
$m = n \times 56.0 = 0.0543 \text{ g}$ (to 3 s.f.)
